qs.q: A 45-year-old woman with chronic diarrhea presents with weakness. Labs: Na⁺ 138 mmol/L, K⁺ 3.0 mmol/L, Cl⁻ 105 mmol/L, HCO₃⁻ 15 mmol/L. What is the likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Anion gap = 138 - (105 + 15) = 18 (normal range). Diarrhea causes bicarbonate loss leading to normal anion gap acidosis. ## Case-Based MCQs Section 2: Kidney Function & Renal Pathology

qs.q: A patient with chronic diarrhea has a pH of 7.25, PaCO₂ 38 mmHg, and HCO₃⁻ 17 mmol/L. What is the acid-base disturbance?
qs.e: Diarrhea causes bicarbonate loss without organic acid accumulation, resulting in normal anion gap metabolic acidosis.

qs.q: A 42-year-old man has weight loss, small joint arthritis, recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, chronic diarrhea with Giardia, hemolytic anemia, and low IgA 70, IgG 303, IgM 64. Normal T cells, slightly reduced B cells. Most likely condition?
qs.e: Low but not absent immunoglobulins + normal T cells + slightly reduced B cells + bacterial and Giardia infections in an adult = common variable immunodeficiency (CVID). B cells cannot differentiate into plasma cells.

qs.q: A 30-year-old man has weight loss, chronic diarrhea, then develops Pneumocystis pneumonia, CMV retinitis, and oral candidiasis. Most likely lab finding?
qs.e: Multiple opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, CMV, Candida) = AIDS. CD4 count below 200/microliter is the threshold at which AIDS-defining opportunistic infections occur in HIV infection.

qs.q: A 44-year-old man has lifelong mild chronic diarrhea and minor respiratory infections. During a blood transfusion after a car accident, he develops an anaphylactic transfusion reaction. Most likely underlying disease?
qs.e: Anaphylaxis during blood transfusion + lifelong mild GI and respiratory issues = selective IgA deficiency. These patients develop anti-IgA antibodies and react anaphylactically to IgA in transfused blood products.
